articles.title: BASE COLOR dropdown
articles.summary: Where the zone colour comes from: Use finish's own color / Use source paint (spec only) / Use solid color / From special / Custom gradient. It is a drop-down menu.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Base.... Range finish | source | solid | special | gradient, starts at finish (new zones); older saves carry an inherited 'source'.
when: "Keep my colours, change only the shine" (source), "make it exactly this colour" (solid), "fade" (gradient).
how: Open the menu and pick a choice.

controls.label: BASE COLOR dropdown
controls.default: finish (new zones); older saves carry an inherited 'source'
controls.effect: Where the zone colour comes from: Use finish's own color / Use source paint...

pitfalls: Solid colour on a finish that brings its own colours (carbon, camo, holographic ...) flattens it to one colour and loses the pattern: use Hue Shift instead. If a colour 'will not apply', check this...

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: finish = the material keeps its own colour; source = KEEP the car's existing paint, change only shine/texture; solid = paint the zone one exact colour; special = take colours from another finish; gradient = 2-10 colour stops across the zone. Applies to: Every base finish and monolithic. It decides where the zone's paint colour comes from.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: Behind the scenes it sets the zone base color mode. It runs over finish | source | solid | special | gradient and starts at finish (new zones); older saves carry an inherited 'source'. Measured in mode.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: A plain 'solid' pick renders the EXACT colour (Color Lab depth/flip/underglow are opt-in; never auto-send base_color_depth). 'source' is spec-only: hue/sat/brightness still adjust the SOURCE colours. MEASURED: solid colour on a monolithic that brings its own palette recolours it but FLATTENS it to one colour (camo structure lost); a hue shift keeps the structure. Picking a mode sets baseColorModeExplicit=true (an unchosen 'source' means 'finish').

protips: Typical values: Wanted colour is exact (hex / 'red') -> pick a base that takes the zone colour and set color:'#rrggbb'. Wanted 'keep my colours, change the shine' -> color:'source' with a Foundation (f_*) finish. Wanted a fade -> gradient with 2-5 stops. On a finish that brings its own palette...

faq.q: What does BASE COLOR dropdown do?
faq.a: Where the zone colour comes from: Use finish's own color / Use source paint (spec only) / Use solid color / From special / Custom gradient.

faq.q: When should I use BASE COLOR dropdown?
faq.a: "Keep my colours, change only the shine" (source), "make it exactly this colour" (solid), "fade" (gradient).

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of BASE COLOR dropdown?
faq.a: Range finish | source | solid | special | gradient. It starts at finish (new zones); older saves carry an inherited 'source'.

faq.q: Why does BASE COLOR dropdown not seem to do what I expect?
faq.a: Solid colour on a finish that brings its own colours (carbon, camo, holographic ...) flattens it to one colour and loses the pattern: use Hue Shift instead. If a colour 'will not apply', check this dropdown first.

combos.why: Works together with the Solid colour swatch / hex control.
Works together with the Hue Shift control.

articles.title: Solid colour swatch / hex

articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE > Base.... Range any #rrggbb, starts at #ffffff.
when: The buyer names an exact colour.
how: Click the colour swatch and pick a colour.

controls.label: Solid colour swatch / hex
controls.effect: Paints the zone this exact colour with the finish's shine on top

pitfalls: Only used when BASE COLOR = Use solid color.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Paints the zone exactly this colour, with the base finish's shine on top. Applies to: Items that take the zone colour (gloss, satin, matte, candy, pearl, metallic, foundation-with-colour). Weak or ignored on monolithics that bring their own palette.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: It runs over any #rrggbb and starts at #ffffff. Measured in hex.

protips: Typical values: Use for any colour the buyer names exactly. For 'pink' use #ff69b4 / hot pink #ff1493 / blush #f4a6c0; always on a base that takes colour.

articles.title: Hue Shift
articles.summary: Rotates every colour around the colour wheel (-180 to +180). It is a slider.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE. Keeps the finish's structure. Range -180..180 (step 1), starts at 0.
when: Recolour a finish that brings its own colours, or tweak a colour a bit.
how: Drag the slider, or click it and use the arrow keys.

controls.label: Hue Shift
controls.effect: Rotates every colour around the colour wheel (-180 to +180)

pitfalls: Shift = target hue minus current hue; +150 on green gives purple, not pink.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Rotates every colour in the zone round the colour wheel. MEASURED: a green (110 deg) zone: +180 -> magenta (311), -150 -> hot pink (338), +150 -> purple (278). Applies to: Everything that renders a base colour: plain bases, monolithics, base+pattern compositions. Does NOT touch the spec (shine).

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: Behind the scenes it sets the zone base hue offset. It runs over -180..180 (step 1) and starts at 0. Measured in degrees around the colour wheel.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: Applied AFTER the colour mode: on 'solid' it shifts the picked colour; on 'finish'/'source' it shifts the material's own / the car's existing colours. Works together with saturation and brightness. Greys (no hue) do not change: a black/white/grey finish needs a colour mode, not hue. Pattern art colours are shifted only if the pattern is painted into the zone paint (overlay mode).

protips: Typical values: Compute shift = target_hue - current_hue, wrapped to -180..180 (hot pink ~335, magenta 310, red 0, orange 30, yellow 60, green 120, cyan 180, blue 230, purple 275). Green camo -> pink = about -150; then saturation +30 and brightness +40 for a lighter vivid pink (measured). Check the...

faq.q: What does Hue Shift do?
faq.a: Rotates every colour around the colour wheel (-180 to +180).

faq.q: When should I use Hue Shift?
faq.a: Recolour a finish that brings its own colours, or tweak a colour a bit.

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Hue Shift?
faq.a: Range -180..180 (step 1). It starts at 0.

faq.q: Why does Hue Shift not seem to do what I expect?
faq.a: Shift = target hue minus current hue; +150 on green gives purple, not pink.

combos.why: Works together with the Saturation control.
Works together with the Brightness control.

articles.title: Saturation
articles.summary: How vivid or grey the colour is (-100 to +100). It is a slider.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE. Range -100..100, starts at 0.
when: Colours look washed out or too loud.
how: Drag the slider, or click it and use the arrow keys.

controls.label: Saturation
controls.effect: How vivid or grey the colour is (-100 to +100)

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Negative = greyer / washed out, positive = more vivid. Applies to: Same as hue shift.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: Behind the scenes it sets the zone base saturation adjust. It runs over -100..100 and starts at 0. Measured in points.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: Pairs with hue: after a big hue shift colours often come out muddy, add +20..40. At -100 the colour is gone.

protips: Typical values: 'pastel / soft' = -20..-40; 'neon / vivid / punchy' = +30..+60; 'desaturate / dull / military' = -40..-70.

faq.q: What does Saturation do?
faq.a: How vivid or grey the colour is (-100 to +100).

faq.q: When should I use Saturation?
faq.a: Colours look washed out or too loud.

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Saturation?
faq.a: Range -100..100. It starts at 0.

combos.why: Works together with the Hue Shift control.

articles.title: Brightness
articles.summary: Lighter or darker (-100 to +200). It is a slider.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE. Range -100..200, starts at 0.
when: Make a colour darker or lighter without changing the finish.
how: Drag the slider, or click it and use the arrow keys.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Negative = darker, positive = lighter (up to double). Applies to: Same as hue shift.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: Behind the scenes it sets the zone base brightness adjust. It runs over -100..200 and starts at 0. Measured in points.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: Brightening a saturated colour desaturates it toward white (pink = red + brightness). Applied after hue/sat.

protips: Typical values: 'lighter / pastel pink' = +30..+80; 'darker / deep' = -20..-50. Hot pink needs hue + saturation more than brightness.

faq.q: What does Brightness do?
faq.a: Lighter or darker (-100 to +200).

faq.q: When should I use Brightness?
faq.a: Make a colour darker or lighter without changing the finish.

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Brightness?
faq.a: Range -100..200. It starts at 0.

combos.why: Works together with the Hue Shift control.

articles.title: Base Strength
articles.summary: Fades the whole base look over the source paint: 0 = original paint, 100 = full finish. It is a slider.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE. Range 0-100%, starts at 100%.
when: A subtle hint of the finish instead of full coverage.
how: Drag the slider, or click it and use the arrow keys.

controls.label: Base Strength
controls.effect: Fades the whole base look over the source paint: 0 = original paint, 100 = full...

pitfalls: This also reduces colour changes; for shine only use Spec Strength.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Fades the complete finish result over the original paint: 0% = the car's own paint, 100% = the full finish. Applies to: Every base / finish.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: It runs over 0-100% and starts at 100%. Measured in %.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: Different from 'intensity' (whole-zone strength preset 10-100) and from spec strength (shine only). Lowering it lets the source paint show through (ghosted finish).

faq.q: What does Base Strength do?
faq.a: Fades the whole base look over the source paint: 0 = original paint, 100 = full finish.

faq.q: When should I use Base Strength?
faq.a: A subtle hint of the finish instead of full coverage.

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Base Strength?
faq.a: Range 0-100%. It starts at 100%.

faq.q: Why does Base Strength not seem to do what I expect?
faq.a: This also reduces colour changes; for shine only use Spec Strength.

combos.why: Works together with the Spec Strength control.

articles.title: Base Scale
articles.summary: Size of the finish's texture inside this zone (0.05x to 5.0x; 1.00x is normal). It is a slider.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE. Smaller = finer, more repeats. Range 0.05x-5.0x (slider 0-1000, 1.00x at the centre; non-linear: left half 0.05-1, right half 1-5), starts at 1.0.
when: Texture too coarse or too fine (carbon, flake, camo look huge on the whole car).
how: Drag the slider, or click it and use the arrow keys.

controls.label: Base Scale
controls.range: 0.05x-5.0x (slider 0-1000, 1.00x at the centre; non-linear: left half 0.05-1, right half 1-5)
controls.effect: Size of the finish's texture inside this zone (0.05x to 5.0x; 1.00x is normal)

pitfalls: Scales the texture, NOT the colours or the whole car; spec follows it unless Independent Spec is ticked.

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Smaller = finer, busier texture (more repeats across the car); larger = bigger grains. 0.5 = twice as fine. Applies to: Base finishes with a visible texture (flake, grain, weave inside the material, fractal / dust). Flat plain bases have no texture to scale.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: Behind the scenes it sets the zone base scale. It runs over 0.05x-5.0x (slider 0-1000, 1.00x at the centre; non-linear: left half 0.05-1, right half 1-5) and starts at 1.0. Measured in x.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: Spec Scale follows Base Scale until 'Independent Spec' is ticked. Does not rescale the whole canvas, only the base texture inside this zone. Not the same control as pattern scale.

protips: Typical values: 'finer flake / tighter grain / crushed to 50%' -> baseScale 0.4-0.6 on the base; 'bigger flake' -> 1.5-3. When the buyer says 'crushed' about a PATTERN, that is the pattern scale instead (zone_pattern_scale).

faq.q: What does Base Scale do?
faq.a: Size of the finish's texture inside this zone (0.05x to 5.0x; 1.00x is normal).

faq.q: When should I use Base Scale?
faq.a: Texture too coarse or too fine (carbon, flake, camo look huge on the whole car).

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Base Scale?
faq.a: Range 0.05x-5.0x (slider 0-1000, 1.00x at the centre; non-linear: left half 0.05-1, right half 1-5). It starts at 1.0.

faq.q: Why does Base Scale not seem to do what I expect?
faq.a: Scales the texture, NOT the colours or the whole car; spec follows it unless Independent Spec is ticked.

combos.why: Works together with the Spec Scale control.

articles.title: Color Depth
articles.summary: For candy / tinted finishes: 0 = no tint, 15 = glaze, 65 = rich, 100 = deepest. It is a slider.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE. Range depth 0-100% (default 65%), flip 0-355 deg, underglow 0-100%, starts at off.
when: Candy looks pale or too dark.
how: Drag the slider, or click it and use the arrow keys.

controls.label: Color Depth
controls.effect: For candy / tinted finishes: 0 = no tint, 15 = glaze, 65 = rich, 100 = deepest

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: Candy-coat look: the colour multiplies over the zone's own structure (depth), a second hue shows in the darks (flip, chameleon feel), a gold/silver ground coat glows through (underglow). Applies to: Zones with a colour mode other than finish/source.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: It runs over depth 0-100% (default 65%), flip 0-355 deg, underglow 0-100% and starts at off. Measured in % / degrees.

protips: Typical values: Only when the buyer asks for candy depth / chameleon / flip colours. Not for an exact colour.

faq.q: What does Color Depth do?
faq.a: For candy / tinted finishes: 0 = no tint, 15 = glaze, 65 = rich, 100 = deepest.

faq.q: When should I use Color Depth?
faq.a: Candy looks pale or too dark.

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Color Depth?
faq.a: Range depth 0-100% (default 65%), flip 0-355 deg, underglow 0-100%. It starts at off.

faq.q: Why does Color Depth not seem to do what I expect?
faq.a: Only shows on candy-like finishes.

articles.title: 2nd Base (picker) + Add 3rd overlay
articles.summary: Pick a second finish blended on top of the primary base; "+ Add 3rd overlay" shows the next slot. It is a colour picker.
articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > OVERLAYS. Range strength 0-100; scale 0.1-5; up to 5 base layers total, starts at none.
how: Click the colour swatch and pick a colour.

controls.label: 2nd Base (picker) + Add 3rd overlay
controls.range: strength 0-100; scale 0.1-5; up to 5 base layers total
controls.effect: Pick a second finish blended on top of the primary base; "+ Add 3rd overlay"...

deep.heading: What it changes
deep.body: A second material blended over the first (e.g. metallic flake over a candy). Applies to: Any zone with a base.

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: It runs over strength 0-100; scale 0.1-5; up to 5 base layers total and starts at none. Measured in layers.

deep.heading: How it combines with other controls
deep.body: Each overlay can carry its own pattern with hue/sat/brightness and its own spec pattern stack. The base overlay's colour is separate from the zone's base colour.

protips: Typical values: 'candy with flake on top' -> base candy + second_base flake at strength 40-70.

faq.q: What does 2nd Base (picker) + Add 3rd overlay do?
faq.a: Pick a second finish blended on top of the primary base; "+ Add 3rd overlay" shows the next slot.

faq.q: When should I use 2nd Base (picker) + Add 3rd overlay?
faq.a: Two-layer looks.

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of 2nd Base (picker) + Add 3rd overlay?
faq.a: Range strength 0-100; scale 0.1-5; up to 5 base layers total. It starts at none.

articles.what: Find it in Pro > ZONE POPOUT PANEL (click a zone card in the left column; Shift+E shows / hides the panel) > BASE (only.... Range scale 0.05-5x; rotation 0-355 deg step 5, starts at 1.0x / 0.

articles.title: Colour strength (zone setting)
articles.summary: How strongly a chosen colour replaces the own colours of the finish. It is a zone setting.
articles.what: Behind the scenes: the app and the AI copilot set this. There is no control for it. Range 0..1, starts at 1. Ignored in finish and source colour modes. The Colour Depth control takes over when the Color Lab is active.
how: Set it in the zone panel.

controls.label: Colour strength (zone setting)
controls.effect: How strongly a chosen colour replaces the own colours of the finish

deep.heading: Under the hood
deep.body: It runs over 0..1 and starts at 1.

faq.q: What does Colour strength (zone setting) do?
faq.a: How strongly a chosen colour replaces the own colours of the finish.

faq.q: What is the range and starting value of Colour strength (zone setting)?
faq.a: Range 0..1. It starts at 1.

articles.title: Exact colour rule (zone setting)
articles.summary: Your colour mode choice is final: source mode keeps your paint and a solid colour stays exact. It is a zone setting.
articles.what: Behind the scenes: the app and the AI copilot set this. There is no control for it. Range n/a, starts at explicit=true; depth absent. Colour depth is only added when you have touched the Color Lab, because depth darkens an exact colour.
how: Set it in the zone panel.
